standard_prerequisites: Chapter lemma-irreducible-polynomials (used by the author without further mention): an irreducible polynomial over a field is separable exactly when its derivative is nonzero, and an irreducible polynomial dividing two polynomials divides their gcd
The minimal polynomial of alpha over E divides the minimal polynomial of alpha over F in E[x] (both vanish at alpha and the F-minimal polynomial lies in E[x])
core_obligations: Let P be the minimal polynomial of alpha over F and Q that over E; then Q divides P in E[x], say P = QR

Differentiate: P' = Q'R + QR'; if Q' = 0 then Q divides both P and P', and the irreducible-polynomials lemma forces P' = 0, contradicting separability of alpha over F; hence Q' != 0 and alpha is separable over E
Part (2): K separable over F means every element of K is separable over F, which is separable over E by (1), which is exactly K separable over E by definition
proof_roadmap: Compare the two minimal polynomials and differentiate the factorization
Read part (2) off part (1) and the definition of a separable extension
